objective: Allow configuration administrators to bind each release approval scenario to a published workflow per project while preserving submission determinism, auditability, and workflow history.

requirements.statement: Configuration management must expose five fixed approval scenarios whose published-workflow bindings are isolated by tenant and project.
acceptance: Project switching loads the corresponding bindings
Each project and scene has at most one binding
Users select a published workflow instead of typing a code
counterexample: A workflow code must be memorized
The binding page edits workflow graphs

requirements.statement: Projects may save partial bindings, while submission must fail atomically only when its resolved scenario is unbound or references a non-published definition.
acceptance: A failed submission creates no round, instance, or status transition
counterexample: A missing emergency binding blocks regular submission
A failed start leaves a STARTING round

requirements.statement: The release backend must resolve the project-scene binding by workflow definition ID and freeze the actual definition version and instance on every submitted round.
acceptance: New submissions use the binding committed at submission time
Existing submissions retain their original definition version after rebinding
The application payload cannot choose a workflow
counterexample: A client-supplied definition ID controls submission

requirements.statement: Binding changes must require a reason, preserve before and after values with operator and time, enforce tenant and project scope, and reject stale writes.
acceptance: Create, update, and unbind history is queryable
Cross-project and cross-tenant access is denied
counterexample: Only the final binding is retained
Concurrent updates silently overwrite each other

requirements.statement: Only never-published definitions with no instances and no active business binding may be deleted, and an actively bound definition may not be archived.
acceptance: A pure draft can be soft-deleted
A formerly published draft cannot be deleted
counterexample: Unpublish then delete bypasses history protection
Archiving a bound definition breaks future submissions

invariants: Running instances retain their original definition and version
All definitions and bindings are tenant scoped
Project context remains a stable interface while mocked
constraints: Preserve the existing workflow lifecycle callback boundary
non_goals: Workflow graph editing from configuration management
Manual workflow choice on a release application

assumptions.text: The current project reference remains stable during this implementation
assumptions.falsifier: The project module changes canonical identifiers without a mapping

assumptions.text: Workflow definition IDs are stable across versions
assumptions.falsifier: Version publication replaces the definition row

unknowns.question: Whether another concurrent migration will claim V43 before integration
unknowns.impact: The migration version may need renumbering without semantic change

measurement_intents.observable: Project-scoped API results and five fixed UI rows
Atomic failure state for unbound and invalid scenes
measurement_intents.candidate_sensor: Submission service tests and database assertions

measurement_intents.observable: Persisted round definition ID, version, and instance before and after rebinding
Delete/archive outcomes under publication, instance, and active-reference states
